```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(p8105.datasets)

library(plotly)
```

#

```{r}
data(nyc_airbnb)

nyc_airbnb = 
  nyc_airbnb |> 
  select(
    neighbourhood_group, neighbourhood, review_scores_location, price, room_type, lat, long) |>
  filter(
    !is.na(review_scores_location), 
    neighbourhood_group == "Manhattan",
    room_type == "Entire home/apt",
    price %in% 100:500)
```


#Plotly 

#Scatterplots
  - ggplot vs plot_ly - define a dataset, how variables map to plot elements,.
```{r}
nyc_airbnb |> 
  mutate(
    text_label = str_c("Price: $", price, "\nRating: ", review_scores_location)
  ) |> 
  plot_ly(
    x = ~lat, y = ~long, type = "scatter", mode = "markers", 
    color = ~price, text = ~text_label, alpha = 0.5
  )

```
- \n shortcut for newline

#Bosplots

```{r}
nyc_airbnb |> 
  mutate(neighbourhood = fct_reorder(neighbourhood, price)) |> 
  plot_ly(y = ~price, color =~neighbourhood,
          type = "box")
```

##barchart

```{r}
nyc_airbnb |> 
  count(neighbourhood) |> 
  mutate(neighbourhood = fct_reorder(neighbourhood, n)) |> 
  plot_ly(x = ~neighbourhood, y =~n, vtype="bar", color = ~neighbourhood,
          colors = "viridis")
```

## ggplotly

```{r}
scatter = nyc_airbnb |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = lat, y = long, color = price)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5)+
  coord_cartesian()

scatter
```
